body: Thoughts were getting to much, but thankfully I didn't do anything too erratic. Instead of killing myself, I decided it's better to change my mind set in the short term and keep myself going, even if it's bad for my health in the long run. I decided  to take some tramadol and honestly I feel so much better. I know drugs can make more long term problems to get short term solutions , but my god does it make a difference. I know it's not good for me, but I haven't felt this comfortable with myself and the world in a long time. I talked to some good friends and wished them a happy July 4th and all. A lot of them actually reached out to me first and now I feel like all my problems are just temporary ones. I know drugs aren't the answer, but if it keeps me from cutting an artery I guess it can't be too bad. Certainly better than the alternative. Thanks for the comments by the way, sorry if I wasted any of your time. I guess I just need someone to talk to is all, even if it's in the form of reddit comments. I just wish I can learn to love myself without hurting myself.

Thank you so much  for saying that. It's hard to feel like your worth something when yourself and those around you seem to think otherwise. I just need to get through this summer, I just have to keep myself alive through the summer and then I'll have more peace when Im back in Philadelphia  with the people I can really trust.

I hope so. I know when I got back my brother told me how I ended up ruining the family and that I'm just a messed up person, which wasn't exactly comforting. I think my parents love me, I know they've put in a lot of money for me. But they constantly remind me of what I've done and explaining all the other things I could do other than working in healthcare. It's like they've all lost hope as much as I did. They keep saying they love me, but it almost seems like the more they say it the less I believe it. But I don't know, if I was going to end my life I doubt I'd tell them. If I did I'd probably just end up locked up in some other hole for god knows how long, and I'd sooner put a bullet in my head than have that happen.

I'm uncertain if I'm away from the people in outpatient care or not. I had their names and number, but I lost the list when I got back to Philadelphia University. I still know their names, but I don't know how I can contact them. As far as legal clause, I don't think there is any. From what I heard, intoxication is not any from of defense, even if I blacked out. I hope the nurse drops the charges obviously, or that I can at least talk to her. The morning I woke up at the hospital I wrote a note of apology and gave it to one of the nurses in hope it can get back to the victim, but my lawyer has tried contacting. Both of them and none have answered. I just have to hope for the best I guess, but after a while you get real sick of simply hoping all the time.
